chapter: 14. Neurocritical Care, Coma, Brain Death & Miscellaneous Neurology
countBasis: Distinct high-yield decisions in the final Neurology chapter; not official exam weighting. Refine after duplication and source review.
boundaries: Avoid repeating standard status drug sequences, stroke reperfusion and spinal emergencies from earlier chapters
Pressure rescue here complements Chapter 13 etiologic pressure syndromes
Label jurisdiction for brain-death standards; US guidance does not replace Indian statutory certification
Critical Care later covers systemic ICU topics in greater depth; retain standalone neurologic care here

decisions: Prioritize airway, ventilation, circulation and bedside glucose in undifferentiated coma
Treat suspected opioid hypoventilation while protecting ventilation
Give thiamine promptly in at-risk patients without delaying hypoglycemia correction
Interpret asymmetric pupils and focal deficits as structural warning signs
Use brainstem examination with trauma and ocular safety precautions
Recognize nonconvulsive seizures as a reversible cause of impaired awareness
Distinguish locked-in syndrome from coma using purposeful vertical eye responses
Use serial standardized examinations and recognize sedation/paralysis confounders

sections.section: Intracranial pressure and traumatic brain injury
decisions: Recognize impending herniation and begin stabilization before definitive imaging or intervention
Use head positioning, venous drainage and oxygenation measures appropriately
Choose hyperosmolar rescue and monitor sodium, renal and hemodynamic consequences
Use brief hyperventilation only as a bridge for a herniation emergency
Apply ICP treatment and cerebral perfusion targets in severe TBI with qualifications
Assess epidural/subdural hematoma deterioration for urgent neurosurgical action
Distinguish CSF diversion and decompression roles according to anatomy
Avoid corticosteroids as treatment for severe TBI
Prevent fever and use contemporary temperature-control guidance without claiming universal deep cooling
Avoid hypoxemia, hypotension and excessive ventilation after ROSC
Treat seizures while interpreting myoclonus with EEG context
Delay prognostic synthesis until appropriate timing and confounder clearance
Use multimodal reliable or moderately reliable predictors rather than one examination sign
Communicate an indeterminate prognosis and avoid self-fulfilling premature withdrawal

sections.section: Brain death clinical prerequisites and examination
decisions: Distinguish death by neurologic criteria from coma and prognosis of severe disability
Establish a permanent catastrophic brain injury with a compatible mechanism
Exclude hypothermia and apply guideline-specific rewarming waiting rules
Exclude sedative intoxication and account for clearance, organ dysfunction and drug levels
Exclude neuromuscular blockade and severe metabolic confounding
Meet blood pressure and physiologic prerequisites under the stated guideline
Assess all required brainstem reflexes and interpret unsafe or untestable components
Interpret spinal reflex movements without mistaking them for brain-mediated activity

sections.section: Apnea testing, ancillary studies and Indian certification
decisions: Prepare safe apnea testing with adequate oxygenation and baseline gases
Apply 2023 US apnea-test PaCO2 and pH endpoints with chronic hypercapnia qualifications
Abort apnea testing for instability and select an appropriate next pathway
Recognize when ancillary testing is justified and when it cannot replace prerequisites
Select accepted perfusion ancillary modalities under the specified guideline
Distinguish EEG electrical silence from the accepted 2023 US ancillary framework
Apply Indian Form 10 adult repeat-testing interval rather than importing a US examination rule
Identify Indian certifying-board requirements and authorized substitution provisions
Keep pediatric certification intervals separate from adult rules and current local requirements
Document certification, family communication and donation independence appropriately

sections.section: Other high-yield neurocritical and behavioral syndromes
decisions: Recognize Wernicke encephalopathy without requiring the complete triad
Recognize posterior reversible encephalopathy and treat the precipitant
Differentiate serotonin syndrome from neuroleptic malignant syndrome
Treat neuroleptic malignant syndrome through withdrawal and supportive escalation
Recognize malignant catatonia and its urgent specialist pathway
Recognize ICU-acquired weakness and distinguish neuropathy/myopathy from CNS nonawakening
Distinguish unresponsive wakefulness from minimally conscious state using repeated assessment
Evaluate functional neurologic symptoms by positive signs while checking acute red flags
